evidence: src/infrastructure/http-app.ts: createApp(service: OrderService) sends every route through service methods (stockLevels, addProduct, placeOrder, listOrders, getOrder, advance, cancel); STATUS and view() are HTTP-specific translation only.
src/infrastructure/http-app.ts: ACTIONS maps route names to target OrderState; the allowed state changes are left to service.advance, so no state-machine rule is duplicated.

src/infrastructure/in-memory-repositories.ts: InMemoryProductRepository implements ProductRepository and InMemoryOrderRepository implements OrderRepository; both are plain Map-backed get/save/list with no business rules.

src/infrastructure/server.ts: builds new OrderService(new InMemoryProductRepository(), new InMemoryOrderRepository()) and calls createApp(service).listen(port), acting as the composition root that uses the module's own pieces.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The infrastructure module is one cohesive concern: the outer adapter layer. http-app.ts is the HTTP adapter and does all its work through the injected OrderService. in-memory-repositories.ts holds the persistence adapters, which implement the application ports with no business logic. server.ts is the composition root that wires them together. No file goes around the module's own pieces: server.ts uses createApp and the repository classes, and http-app.ts never touches the repositories directly. No rule is duplicated. ACTIONS only maps URL action names to target states, and the allowed state changes stay inside service.advance. The 'items must be an array' check in POST /orders is a request-shape check before the cast to OrderLine[], not a restated domain rule. Mixing the startup wiring with the adapters is a common, acceptable pattern rather than a cohesion fault.
